post.post_content:
DreamHost is an independently owned host with a clear price list: it shows the renewal price next to the first-term price. The cheapest plan hosts 25 websites. The catch is that the low price needs a long term, and email is free for only three months. This page puts the prices, the limits, the test results and the WordPress setup in one place. Prices were read on DreamHost's own pages on 20 November 2026.

Is DreamHost worth it? The short version

  • The term decides the price. Launch is $2.89 a month on a 1-year term and renews at $10.99. On a 4-year term it is $1.99 and renews at $7.99.
  • Lots of sites for the money. Launch allows 25 websites with 25 GB of NVMe storage and daily backups.
  • Speed is average. In WPBeginner's July 2026 tests DreamHost loaded in 986 ms, and Hostinger in 659 ms.
  • No phone support. Support is 24/7 chat and tickets.
  • The refund window is 30 days. Older reviews that say 97 days describe plans DreamHost no longer sells.

How much does DreamHost cost?

DreamHost sells three shared WordPress hosting plans: Launch, Growth and Scale. The prices below are the first-year prices on DreamHost's pricing page, read on 20 November 2026. DreamHost says the full term plus taxes is charged at checkout.

LaunchGrowthScale
First year, a month$2.89$3.99$9.99
Renews at, a month, after a 1-year term$10.99$12.99$25.99
4-year term, a month$1.99$3.49$7.99
Renews at, a month, after a 4-year term$7.99$8.99$19.99
Websites2550100
Storage25 GB NVMe50 GB NVMe100 GB NVMe
DreamHost's monthly visit estimate40,000200,000400,000
Mailboxes, free for 3 months204060

The renewal figures and the 4-year prices come from DreamHost's reviews page and from WPThinker, which checked the plan pages on 7 November 2026. Month-to-month billing is $4.99 for the first 3 months, then $11.99, according to DreamHost. The visit numbers are estimates for each plan, not hard limits. Bandwidth is unmetered.

[[cta: See DreamHost plans | A 30-day money-back guarantee applies. Check the term and the renewal in your cart.]]

How much does DreamHost cost after the first year?

At DreamHost the renewal price depends on the length of your first term. A longer first term gives a lower renewal. We worked out two five-year paths for the Launch plan. This is our own arithmetic from the prices above, and it assumes you renew each year at the quoted rate.

PathFirst termNext yearsFive-year totalAverage a month
4-year term, then 1 year at $7.99$95.52$95.88$191.40$3.19
1-year term, then 4 yearly renewals at $10.99$34.68$527.52$562.20$9.37

The renewal is 4.0 times the first price on the 4-year term, 3.8 times on the 1-year term and 2.4 times on the month-to-month route. If you are sure you will stay, the 4-year term saves money twice. If you are not sure, the 30-day guarantee gives you a way out.

What do you get with DreamHost?

  • Daily automated backups on all three plans, a free SSL certificate, unmetered bandwidth and a free domain for the first year.
  • An AI website builder, called Liftoff, and on-demand performance scans.
  • A 100% uptime guarantee. If DreamHost misses it, you get one day of hosting credit for each hour of downtime, up to 10% of your next renewal.
  • A custom control panel, not cPanel.

Some features are missing on the shared plans. DreamHost says you need DreamPress for the CDN and one-click staging. Email is free for the first 3 months only. After that it costs from $1.67 a month for one mailbox on annual billing, or from $1.99 on monthly billing, according to WPRoom.

DreamHost nonprofit hosting: is it free?

DreamHost offers a nonprofit discount. According to DreamHost's help article as summarized by TechEMPOWER (checked May 2026), a US 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(19) nonprofit can get one free shared hosting plan for the life of its account, with email hosting, SSL and a free domain for the first year. It also lists 35% off DreamPress. The IRS determination letter is the only proof DreamHost accepts. The free plan is for the nonprofit's own sites only. Terms can change, so check DreamHost's help page before you apply.

What is DreamPress, and do you need it?

DreamPress is DreamHost's managed WordPress plan. DreamPress 1 was $14.99 a month in the first year and renews at $19.99. It covers 1 website, 15 GB of NVMe storage, 40,000 monthly visits and 14 days of backups. It adds the CDN, staging and the managed features. Launch hosts 25 sites for far less, so DreamPress only makes sense for one important site that needs those extras. WPSchool measured DreamPress at 268 ms time to first byte against 487 ms for shared hosting on its older test plan.

Is DreamHost good for WordPress?

Yes for blogs, small business sites and several small sites on one plan. The shared plans give you many sites, NVMe storage and daily backups. WPSchool installed WordPress with WooCommerce and seven plugins on its test site and ran it for 30 days. The limits are no staging or CDN on shared plans, and a first response that trails LiteSpeed hosts. If you want WordPress set up and kept running for you, our website maintenance service covers updates, backups and speed checks on any host.

How fast is DreamHost? What independent tests found

We did not run our own speed or uptime test. Independent teams did. They used different plans, so we list each with its method.

TestSpeed resultUptime
WPBeginner, tests in July 2026. Same WordPress site on 15 hosts, GTmetrix, 6 regions986 ms Largest Contentful Paint, 658 ms average response. Score 64 out of 100, against 88 for Hostinger100% over 30 days
hosttest.de, February 2026. Launch plan, monthly billing0.133 s time to first byte, 1.5 s Largest Contentful Paint100%
WPSchool, April 2026. Older Shared Unlimited plan, WooCommerce test site, 30 days, 50 users487 ms time to first byte. It rose to 800 to 950 ms under 50 concurrent users99.97%

The pattern is steady. DreamHost is fast enough for most small sites in the US and slower than LiteSpeed hosts. The WPSchool numbers come from a plan DreamHost has since replaced, so treat them as a guide. The shared plans have no server-level caching, so a caching plugin helps. Google treats a Largest Contentful Paint of 2.5 seconds or less as good.

[[cta: Test it on your own site | You have 30 days to check speed and support and cancel for a refund.]]

How is DreamHost support?

  • Channels: 24/7 live chat and tickets. There is no phone line. WPRoom says a one-time callback costs $9.95.
  • Wait times: HostingAdvice reported live chat waits of about 30 minutes in its hands-on test.
  • Languages: WPRoom lists English and Spanish.

Where are DreamHost's data centers?

In late October 2026, WPThinker saw data centers in Oregon, Virginia and Amsterdam. An April 2026 review said the US only, so the list may have grown. If most of your visitors are in Asia or Australia, a host with servers closer to them may be quicker.

Is the DreamHost 97-day guarantee still real?

No, not for new plans. Older reviews praise a 97-day money-back guarantee. DreamHost's current pricing page says 30 days. RankPlot reported in June 2026 that DreamHost retired the older Shared Starter and Shared Unlimited plans for new buyers. Plan for 30 days.

DreamHost pros and cons

Pros

  • 25 websites and 25 GB of NVMe storage on the cheapest plan.
  • Daily backups, free SSL and a free domain for the first year.
  • A 100% uptime guarantee with hosting credits.
  • Renewal prices are shown next to the first-term prices.
  • A free shared plan for eligible US nonprofits.

Cons

  • The cheapest price needs a 4-year term, and the renewal is 3.8 to 4.0 times higher.
  • Email is free for only 3 months.
  • No staging or CDN on shared plans.
  • No phone support.
  • Speed trails LiteSpeed hosts in the tests we read.
  • DreamPress costs much more than Launch.

DreamHost vs Bluehost and Hostinger

WPBeginner tested these hosts the same way in July 2026. The figures are WPBeginner's.

Largest Contentful PaintAverage responseUptime, 30 daysScore out of 100
Hostinger659 ms227 ms100%88
Bluehost933 ms599 ms100%69
DreamHost986 ms658 ms100%64

DreamHost allows more sites on its entry plan than Bluehost (25 against 10) and than Hostinger Premium (3). It was slower in these tests. Read our Hostinger review and our Bluehost review, or see all options in our best web hosting services list.

Who should use DreamHost, and who should look elsewhere?

DreamHost suits: bloggers and small businesses with several small sites, freelancers with client sites, eligible US nonprofits, and anyone who wants the renewal price shown up front.

Look elsewhere if: you need phone support, you want staging and a CDN on a budget plan, speed is your top priority, or most of your visitors are far from the US and Europe. Our best cloud hosting page covers managed cloud servers.

How do you build a WordPress site on DreamHost? Step by step

  1. Choose a plan and a term. Launch covers 25 sites. A 4-year term has the lowest renewal.
  2. Register your free domain. It is free for the first year. Check what it costs to renew.
  3. Create your account and check the cart. Note the email trial, which becomes a paid plan after 3 months.
  4. Install WordPress. Use DreamHost's panel to add WordPress to your domain. If you have a site elsewhere, ask about the free WordPress migration.
  5. Add caching. Shared plans have no server-level cache, so install a caching plugin.
  6. Pick a theme and add pages. Add a home page, an about page and a contact page first. Then set up SEO and security plugins.
  7. Check backups and set a renewal reminder. Backups are daily. Add the renewal date and the new price to your calendar.

Which DreamHost plan should you pick?

  • A blog or a few small sites: Launch.
  • More sites and more traffic: Growth.
  • A busy agency or store: Scale.
  • One important site that needs staging and a CDN: DreamPress.

Final verdict: is DreamHost worth it in 2026?

Yes, if you want many small sites on one cheap plan and you will commit to a long term. Pick the 4-year term only if you are sure, budget for email after three months, and use the 30-day window to test it. Skip it if you need phone support or the fastest speed.

Our interest in this topic

Reinforce Lab builds and maintains WordPress sites. We may earn a commission when you buy hosting through links on this page. We do not host our own site on DreamHost, so this is a research-based review. We read the host's pages and published tests, and we did not run our own. We do not sell hosting ourselves. How we researched this page is in the panel above.
